subject: music
title: Screen Score Stretch: Interactive & Adaptive Music
welcome_lead: How does music react in real time to gameplay? Step into the cutting edge of adaptive scoring.
meta_desc: GCSE Music Film & Game Music Adventure 3: stretch into adaptive music, vertical layering, horizontal re-sequencing and modern scoring.
final_note: You understand how game music thinks and reacts — far beyond simple background loops.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Vertical layering lets game music react without changing tracks. Calm exploration might use just strings and piano; when enemies appear, drums and brass layer on top.

The pulse stays continuous, so transitions feel seamless. Games like The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild use this beautifully.

walkthroughs.h2: Switching tracks at the right moment
walkthroughs.body_html:
Horizontal re-sequencing swaps to a different track when the situation changes — combat to victory, day to night. The audio engine waits for a musically smart point (end of bar/phrase) so the switch feels natural.

This avoids the jarring 'cut' that would happen with a simple cross-fade.

For film, composer and director do a spotting session — watching the cut to decide which scenes need music. Each cue is then composed to fit precisely.

In games, stingers (short stings like a sword-hit chord) add reactivity without interrupting the underscore — small moments of musical feedback for the player.
